problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis in the direction of decreasing $x$ where $x>0.$ When the displacement of $P$ from the origin $O$ is $x\,m,$ its velocity is $v\,m/s$ and its acceleration is $4(1+2x)\,{m/s}^{2}.$ If $P$ has a displacement of $1\,m$ when its velocity is $-4\,m/s,$ find $v$ in terms of $x.$

activity_context.topic_title: Velocity and Acceleration as Functions of Displacement

feedback.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis in the direction of increasing $x.$ When the displacement of $P$ from the origin $O$ is $x\,m,$ its velocity is $v\,m/s$ and its acceleration is $(2x+1)\,{m/s}^{2}.$ If $P$ has a displacement of $1\,m$ when its velocity is $4\,m/s,$ find $v$ in terms of $x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14070816/assets/983beaf02582c5ebaee129e28bba657eb2db5e4da7f74eb4b8eba73b9083a259.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ is $(2x+1)\,{m/s}^{2},$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=2x+1.
$$

Using the fact that 

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}),
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=2x+1.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x=\int (2x+1)\,\text{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}={x}^{2}+x+C.
$$

Now, since $x=1\,\text{m}$ when $v=4\,\text{m/s},$ we can find the value of the constant $C$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & ={x}^{2}+x+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(4)^{2} & ={1}^{2}+1+C \\ 8 & =2+C \\ C & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & ={x}^{2}+x+6 \\ {v}^{2} & =2({x}^{2}+x+6) \\ v & =\pm \sqrt{2({x}^{2}+x+6)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the particle is moving in the direction of increasing  $x,$ we have that $v(x)>0,$ so we can discard the negative square root. Therefore,

$$
v(x)=\sqrt{2({x}^{2}+x+6)}.
$$
